chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid and ʿAli ibn al-Nuʿman, from Ibn Muskan, who said:

I asked Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who performed tamattuʿ and did not find a sacrificial offering. He said: He should fast three days. I said to him: Are the Days of Tashriq included among them? He said: No, but he should remain in Mecca until he fasts them, and seven when he returns to his family. If his companions do not remain for him and he is unable to stay in Mecca, then let him fast ten days when he returns to his family. And he mentioned the hadith of Budayl ibn Warqaʾ.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: the designated days after Eid during which these three fasts are not observed
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the total substitute fast of ten days in place of the offering
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering required in the pilgrimage context
key_terms.يُقِيمُ بِمَكَّةَ: he remains in Mecca to complete the required fasting

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ do if he cannot find a sacrificial offering?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the ruling for one performing Hajj al-tamattuʿ who cannot find the required sacrificial animal. He must fast three days, excluding the Days of Tashriq, and then seven more upon returning to his family; if he cannot remain in Mecca, he may fast all ten after returning home.
